runtime_investigation: Runtime 47.812s and Passed: 2421 both sit outside the range of most stored logs (~3m16s, 2518-2728 assertions), so I chased this down rather than waving at load noise. It localises to three tests: epoll01 51.83s -> 1.481s, fcntl14 41.60s -> 1.196s, fcntl14_64 41.58s -> 1.185s, which account for ~131s of the ~148s gap; all three still pass. The cause is the build profile, not this patch. Evidence: run-f6fYXT's saved full suite, the one prior log whose verify.json documents a RELEASE=1 invocation, reports Runtime 48.161s, Passed 2392, epoll01 1.536s, fcntl14 1.262s, fcntl14_64 1.263s -- matching mine within noise, while the ~3m runs (verify-iIbwju: epoll01 52.456s, 2667 passed; verify-nQNo7j: 53.104s, 2580 passed) are the debug ones. fcntl14 is 5000 fork+lock iterations over 2 variants and epoll01 is likewise syscall-bound, exactly the shape that a release kernel collapses. Also ruled out the base commit: 25 other runs share base_commit e8f2b9ca6 and show the slow numbers, so the base cannot explain it. Independently reproduced with a selector boot on the patched kernel (epoll01 1.481s, fcntl14 1.190s, fcntl14_64 1.187s, ioctl01 pass, exit 0), identical to the full-suite figures. The assertion count tracks the profile for the same reason and 2421 vs f6fYXT's 2392 is a 29-assertion spread on a like-for-like comparison.
